Back Squat.cue: Brace, sit between the hips, drive the floor away.
Back Squat.howTo: Setup: Bar sits across your upper back (not your neck), feet shoulder-width, toes turned out a little. Take a big belly breath and brace like you are about to be poked in the stomach. Move: Sit down between your hips until your thighs are about parallel, then push the floor away to stand. Watch for: Knees caving in, heels lifting, or your chest dropping forward. Tip: If you cannot reach depth with a flat back, use a lighter load or the box version first.

Front Squat.howTo: Setup: Rest the bar on your front shoulders with elbows high, or hold weights at your chest. Feet shoulder-width. Move: Sit straight down while keeping your chest tall, then stand. The upright torso makes this squat hit the quads hard. Watch for: Elbows dropping, which rounds your upper back. Tip: Wrist or shoulder stiff? Cross your arms over the bar or use the goblet position instead.

Pause Squat.cue: Hold the bottom for 2 seconds, stay tight, then stand.
Pause Squat.howTo: Setup: Same stance as a regular squat. Move: Lower under control, stay tight and hold the bottom for the stated count, then stand up. Do not bounce or relax in the hole. The pause teaches you to own the bottom position. Watch for: Losing your brace or letting the back round while paused. Tip: Use about 10 to 20 percent less weight than your normal squat.

Box Squat.cue: Sit back to the box, stay tight, stand without rocking.
Box Squat.howTo: Setup: Place a box or bench behind you at about knee height. Move: Sit back to the box with control, touch it lightly (do not crash or rock), then stand up by pushing through your whole foot. Watch for: Collapsing onto the box or rocking back to build momentum. Tip: Great for learning depth and for anyone with knee or hip discomfort because the box gives you a consistent target.

Tempo Squat.cue: Lower slowly, drive up at normal speed.
Tempo Squat.howTo: Setup: Regular squat stance and brace. Move: Take the full count to lower (for example 3 to 4 seconds), then stand at normal speed. Slow lowering builds control and muscle without needing heavy weight. Watch for: Dropping fast at the end of the count. Tip: Count out loud in your head. If the last reps get shaky, stop the set rather than rushing.

Goblet Squat.cue: Hold the weight at the chest with elbows inside the knees.
Goblet Squat.howTo: Setup: Hold one weight against your chest with both hands, elbows pointing down. Feet a little wider than your hips. Move: Sit between your knees, keeping your chest tall and your elbows inside your knees, then stand. Watch for: Heels lifting and the weight drifting away from your body. Tip: The best first squat to learn. If it feels easy, slow it down rather than rushing to heavier weight.

Leg Press.cue: Use full range and keep the hips down.
Leg Press.howTo: Setup: Sit back in the seat with your whole back and hips flat against the pad. Feet shoulder-width on the platform, mid-height. Move: Lower until your knees are bent about 90 degrees, then push the platform away without locking your knees hard. Watch for: Hips curling off the seat at the bottom. Tip: Always use the safety stops and never bounce the weight off your chest. If you have no machine the wall sit does the same job.

Hack Squat.cue: Control the lowering and keep the front foot flat.
Hack Squat.howTo: Setup: Stand on the platform with your back flat against the pad and feet shoulder-width, slightly forward. Move: Lower until your thighs are about parallel, keeping your whole foot flat, then press back up. Watch for: Heels lifting or knees collapsing inward. Tip: Move slowly on the way down so the quads do the work, not momentum.

Split Squat.cue: Stay tall and drop the back knee straight down.
Split Squat.howTo: Setup: Take a long stance with one foot forward and the other behind, feet hip-width apart side to side like on train tracks. Move: Drop your back knee straight down toward the floor, keeping your torso tall, then push through the front foot to rise. Stay in the same spot; no stepping. Watch for: Front heel lifting or the stance being too short. Tip: Hold a wall or rail for balance until it feels steady.

Bulgarian Split Squat.cue: Rear foot on a bench, lean slightly forward, drive through the front heel.
Bulgarian Split Squat.howTo: Setup: Stand about two feet in front of a bench and rest the top of your back foot on it. Move: Lower straight down until your front thigh is near parallel, leaning slightly forward, then drive through the front heel. Watch for: Standing too close to the bench, which pushes the knee over the toes and strains it. Tip: Start with bodyweight. This one is hard and humbling, and that is normal.

Walking Lunge.cue: Long steps, torso upright, no bouncing off the knee.
Walking Lunge.howTo: Setup: Stand tall with feet together. Move: Take a long step forward, drop the back knee toward the floor, then push through the front foot and bring the back leg through into the next step. Watch for: Short steps, a leaning torso, or bouncing off the back knee. Tip: Take your time and keep your eyes up. If balance is tricky, use the reverse lunge or split squat instead.

Reverse Lunge.cue: Step back softly and push through the front foot.
Reverse Lunge.howTo: Setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width. Move: Step one foot back and lower the back knee toward the floor, then push through the front foot to return. Stepping back is easier on the knees than stepping forward. Watch for: A tiny step, which loads the knee, and a front heel lifting. Tip: Hold a wall or rail for balance if you are new.

Step-Up.cue: Use a box that puts the knee near hip height and avoid pushing off the back foot.
Step-Up.howTo: Setup: Face a box or sturdy step that puts your knee near hip height when your foot is on top. Move: Put your whole foot on the box, then stand up by driving through that front leg. Lower slowly with the same leg. Watch for: Pushing off the bottom foot, which cheats the exercise. Tip: Choose a lower step if you cannot control the way down.

Lateral Lunge.cue: Sit back into one hip and keep the other leg straight.
Lateral Lunge.howTo: Setup: Stand tall with feet together. Move: Take a big step out to the side, sit back into that hip while the other leg stays straight, then push back to the start. Your chest stays up and both feet point forward. Watch for: Turning the toes out or rounding your back. Tip: This works the inner thigh and glutes and loosens tight hips.

Deadlift.cue: Bar over mid-foot, flat back, push the floor away.
Deadlift.howTo: Setup: Stand with the bar over the middle of your feet, feet hip-width. Hinge down and grip just outside your legs. Pull your chest up so your back is flat and your shoulders are slightly in front of the bar. Move: Push the floor away and stand tall, bar sliding up your legs. Reverse the path to lower. Watch for: A rounded back, jerking the bar off the floor, or hyper-extending at the top. Tip: Film a set from the side to check your back. Lighter and perfect beats heavier and sloppy.

Trap Bar Deadlift.cue: Stand tall at the top and keep the weight close.
Trap Bar Deadlift.howTo: Setup: Step inside the hex bar, feet hip-width, and grab the handles. Hips down, chest up, back flat. Move: Push the floor away and stand tall with the weight at your sides. Lower with control. Watch for: Letting your hips shoot up first, which turns it into a back lift. Tip: The most beginner-friendly deadlift because the weight stays beside your body.

Deficit Deadlift.cue: Stand on a 1 to 2 inch plate and keep the back flat at the start.
Deficit Deadlift.howTo: Setup: Stand on a 1 to 2 inch plate or low platform, set up like a normal deadlift. Move: Because you start lower, you must stay extra tight; push the floor away and stand tall. Watch for: Losing back position in the first inch. Tip: Use about 10 to 20 percent less weight than your regular deadlift.

Pause Deadlift.cue: Pause for 2 seconds just below the knee, then finish the pull.
Pause Deadlift.howTo: Setup: Regular deadlift setup. Move: Pull up until the bar passes the knee, hold for 2 seconds while keeping your back flat, then finish the lift. Watch for: Standing up early or letting the back round during the pause. Tip: The pause teaches you where your weak spot is. Keep the weight light.

Sumo Deadlift.cue: Wide stance, knees out, chest tall.
Sumo Deadlift.howTo: Setup: Take a wide stance with toes turned out and grab the bar with arms inside your legs. Hips low, chest tall. Move: Spread the floor apart with your feet, push your knees out and stand tall. Watch for: Knees caving in and hips shooting up first. Tip: A good option if your back or hips feel more comfortable with a wide stance.

Romanian Deadlift.cue: Push the hips back, soft knees, feel the hamstrings stretch.
Romanian Deadlift.howTo: Setup: Stand tall with the weight in front of your thighs, knees slightly bent. Move: Push your hips straight back as if closing a car door with your butt. Let the weight slide down your legs until you feel a strong stretch in the hamstrings, then squeeze your glutes to stand. Watch for: Bending your knees more as you go down (that turns it into a squat) or rounding your back. Tip: The weight should skim your legs the whole way.

Good Morning.cue: Hands on the shoulders or behind the head, hinge with a flat back.
Good Morning.howTo: Setup: Hands on your shoulders or behind your head (or the bar across your upper back). Feet hip-width, soft knees. Move: Hinge your hips back with a flat back until your torso is near parallel, then squeeze the glutes to stand. Watch for: Rounding the back or locking the knees. Tip: Start with bodyweight and master the hinge before adding load.

Hip Thrust.cue: Chin tucked, ribs down, squeeze the glutes at the top.
Hip Thrust.howTo: Setup: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and the weight across your hips (or none for bodyweight). Feet flat, shoulder-width. Move: Drive your hips up until your torso is flat from shoulders to knees. Squeeze your glutes hard for a second, then lower. Chin stays tucked and ribs down. Watch for: Arching your low back at the top instead of using your glutes. Tip: Shins should be vertical at the top. If you feel it in your back, tuck your pelvis more.

Back Extension.cue: Lift to a straight line and avoid over-arching.
Back Extension.howTo: Setup: Lie face down on the bench with your hips just off the pad and ankles anchored, hands across your chest. Move: Lower your torso down, then lift until your body is in one straight line. Squeeze your glutes at the top. Watch for: Swinging up and arching past straight. Tip: No bench? The floor Superman hold does a similar job.

Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift.cue: Hips square, reach long, slight bend in the standing knee.
Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift.howTo: Setup: Stand on one leg with a soft knee, weight in the opposite hand (or none). Move: Hinge your hips back and reach the free leg straight behind you, keeping your hips square to the floor. Lower until you feel the hamstring stretch, then squeeze your glute to stand. Watch for: Twisting open at the hip or rounding your back. Tip: Touch a wall with your free hand for balance when starting out.

Kettlebell Swing.cue: Snap the hips and let the arms float.
Kettlebell Swing.howTo: Setup: Stand with feet a bit wider than your shoulders and the weight on the floor a foot in front of you. Hinge back, hike it between your legs like a football. Move: Snap your hips forward hard and let the weight float to chest height with straight arms. Let it fall back and hinge again. Watch for: Squatting it up, or lifting with your arms or shoulders. Tip: The hips do the work; your arms are just ropes. Stop the set when form slips.

Leg Curl.howTo: Setup: Adjust the machine so the pad sits just above your heels and your knees line up with the pivot. Move: Curl your heels toward your glutes, pause, then lower slowly for 2 to 3 seconds. Watch for: Lifting your hips off the seat or using momentum. Tip: No machine? The slider or Nordic curl works the same muscle.

Calf Raise.cue: Pause at the top and stretch at the bottom.
Calf Raise.howTo: Setup: Stand with the balls of your feet on a step or the pads, heels hanging off. Move: Lower your heels for a deep stretch, then press up as high as you can onto your toes and pause for a second. Watch for: Bouncing quickly or cutting the range short. Tip: Slow reps beat heavy, bouncy reps for calves.

Bench Press.cue: Shoulder blades pinched, feet planted, bar to the lower chest.
Bench Press.howTo: Setup: Lie back with your eyes under the bar, feet planted, shoulder blades squeezed together and slightly arched upper back. Grip a little wider than your shoulders. Move: Lower the bar to your lower chest under control, then press it up and slightly back over your shoulders. Watch for: Bouncing the bar, flaring your elbows wide, or lifting your hips. Tip: Use a spotter or the safety bars. For beginners, the dumbbell version is easier to learn.

Pause Bench Press.cue: Pause on the chest for 1 to 2 seconds, then press.
Pause Bench Press.howTo: Setup: Set up as for a normal bench press: feet planted, shoulder blades squeezed together, bar over your eyes. Move: Lower the bar to your chest under control, hold it still for 1 to 2 seconds without relaxing your upper back, then press up. Watch for: Sinking into your chest or bouncing out of the pause. Tip: Use about 10 to 20 percent less than your usual bench. The pause removes the bounce and teaches you to be strong off the chest. Use a spotter.

Incline Bench Press.howTo: Setup: Set the bench to about 30 degrees. Lie back with your feet planted and shoulder blades squeezed. Move: Lower the bar to your upper chest and press up. Watch for: Setting the bench too steep, which turns it into a shoulder press. Tip: Works the upper chest.

Close-Grip Bench Press.cue: Hands just inside shoulder width, elbows tucked.
Close-Grip Bench Press.howTo: Setup: Lie back as for a bench press but grip with hands just inside shoulder width. Move: Lower with elbows tucked close to your ribs, then press. Watch for: Gripping too narrow, which strains the wrists. Tip: Builds triceps and tends to feel friendlier on shoulders.

Floor Press.cue: Pause the triceps on the floor, then press.
Floor Press.howTo: Setup: Lie on the floor with knees bent, holding the weight over your chest. Move: Lower until your triceps touch the floor, pause, then press. Watch for: Crashing your elbows into the floor. Tip: The floor limits the range, so it is shoulder-friendly and needs no bench.

Dumbbell Bench Press.cue: Lower until the elbows are slightly below the bench.
Dumbbell Bench Press.howTo: Setup: Sit with the dumbbells on your thighs, lie back and kick them up to chest level. Feet planted, shoulder blades squeezed. Move: Lower until your elbows are just below the bench, then press up and slightly together. Watch for: Flaring elbows wide or dropping too fast. Tip: Pick a weight you can control for all reps. Dumbbells let each arm work on its own.

Incline Dumbbell Press.howTo: Setup: Set the bench to about 30 degrees. Sit with the dumbbells on your thighs, lie back, and kick them up to chest level. Feet planted, shoulder blades squeezed. Move: Press the weights up and slightly together until your arms are straight, then lower until your elbows are just below the bench line. Watch for: A steep bench that turns it into a shoulder press, or your low back peeling off the pad. Tip: This is the best upper chest move for most people. Choose a weight you can control for every rep.

Push-Up.cue: Body in one line, chest to the floor.
Push-Up.howTo: Setup: Hands under your shoulders, body in one straight line from head to heels, glutes squeezed. Move: Lower your chest to the floor with elbows at about 45 degrees to your body, then press away until your arms lock out. Watch for: Sagging hips, flared elbows, or half reps. Tip: Too hard? Do them on a bench, countertop or knees and work down.

Dips.cue: Shoulders down, lean slightly forward for chest.
Dips.howTo: Setup: Grip the parallel bars with straight arms, shoulders pulled down away from your ears. Move: Lower until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor, leaning forward slightly for more chest, then press up. Watch for: Shoulders rolling forward or dropping too deep. Tip: Use the bench dip or assisted version until you build strength.

Chest Fly.cue: Soft elbows, stretch wide, hug the weight in.
Chest Fly.howTo: Setup: Lie back holding light weights (or stand at cables) with a slight bend in your elbows. Move: Open your arms wide until you feel a stretch across the chest, then hug the weights back together. Watch for: Locking the elbows or going too heavy. Tip: Light weights, slow reps.

Overhead Press.cue: Squeeze the glutes and press the bar in a straight line.
Overhead Press.howTo: Setup: Hold the bar at your collarbone, grip just outside shoulders, elbows slightly in front of the bar. Glutes and abs tight. Move: Press the bar straight up, moving your head back then through as it passes the face, until your arms lock out over your ears. Lower with control. Watch for: Leaning back and arching the low back. Tip: Squeeze your glutes the whole time. Start with dumbbells if the bar feels awkward.

Push Press.cue: Dip and drive with the legs, then finish with the arms.
Push Press.howTo: Setup: Bar or dumbbells at your shoulders, feet hip-width. Move: Dip a few inches by bending your knees, then drive up with the legs and finish pressing the weight overhead. Lower to the shoulders and reset. Watch for: Dipping forward or pressing early. Tip: The legs start the movement, the shoulders finish it, so you can handle more than a strict press.

Seated Dumbbell Press.cue: Keep the ribs down and press slightly in.
Seated Dumbbell Press.howTo: Setup: Sit with your back supported, dumbbells at shoulder height, elbows slightly in front. Move: Press the weights up until your arms are straight, then lower to ear level. Watch for: Arching off the pad. Tip: A great first shoulder press because the seat removes balance and leg drive.

Landmine Press.cue: Press up and forward and keep the ribs down.
Landmine Press.howTo: Setup: Wedge one end of a barbell in a corner or landmine. Hold the other end at your shoulder with one hand. Move: Press the end up and forward on a diagonal until your arm is straight, then lower. Watch for: Twisting your body. Tip: Often the easiest overhead press on your shoulders because of the angle.

Arnold Press.howTo: Setup: Sit with your back supported, holding dumbbells at chest height with palms facing you. Move: Press up while rotating your palms to face forward, finishing with arms straight overhead. Reverse the rotation as you lower. Watch for: Rushing the turn or arching your back. Tip: Use lighter dumbbells than your normal press. The rotation hits all three parts of the shoulder.

Lateral Raise.cue: Lead with the elbows to shoulder height.
Lateral Raise.howTo: Setup: Stand holding light dumbbells at your sides, a slight bend in the elbows. Move: Raise your arms out to the side until they reach shoulder height, as if pouring out two jugs, then lower slowly. Watch for: Shrugging or swinging. Tip: Go lighter than you think. If you need to swing it, it is too heavy.

Barbell Row.cue: Hinge to about 45 degrees and pull to the lower ribs.
Barbell Row.howTo: Setup: Hold the bar with a shoulder-width grip, hinge your hips back until your torso is at about 45 degrees, flat back, soft knees. Move: Pull the bar to your lower ribs, squeezing shoulder blades together, then lower. Watch for: Standing up as you pull or rounding your back. Tip: If your back tires first, use a chest-supported row.

Pendlay Row.cue: Reset on the floor each rep and keep the back flat.
Pendlay Row.howTo: Setup: Torso parallel to the floor, bar resting on the floor between reps. Move: Pull the bar explosively to your lower chest, then lower it to the floor and reset. Watch for: Using your hips to jerk it. Tip: Resetting each rep lets your back rest, which makes it easier to keep good form.

Dumbbell Row.cue: Pull the elbow to the hip without twisting.
Dumbbell Row.howTo: Setup: Put one hand and the same-side knee on a bench, other foot on the floor, flat back. Move: Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, elbow close to your side, then lower fully. Watch for: Twisting your torso to lift. Tip: Think of pulling with your elbow, not your hand.

Chest-Supported Row.cue: Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
Chest-Supported Row.howTo: Setup: Lie face down on an incline bench with the weights hanging. Move: Row the weights toward your ribs, squeeze, and lower under control. Watch for: Lifting your chest off the pad. Tip: The bench removes the low back, so it is great for beginners.

Seated Cable Row.cue: Chest tall and pull to the belly button.
Seated Cable Row.howTo: Setup: Sit tall with knees slightly bent, arms straight holding the handle. Move: Pull the handle to your belly button, squeezing shoulder blades together, then let your arms extend while keeping your chest tall. Watch for: Rocking back to yank the weight. Tip: Pause for a second at the end of each rep.

Face Pull.cue: Pull to the face with elbows high and thumbs back.
Face Pull.howTo: Setup: Set a cable at forehead height with a rope. Step back with arms extended. Move: Pull the rope toward your face, splitting it apart so your hands end beside your ears with elbows high. Watch for: Leaning back or going heavy. Tip: Light weight; this protects your shoulders and improves posture.

Rear Delt Fly.cue: Small arc, lead with the elbows.
Rear Delt Fly.howTo: Setup: Hinge forward with a flat back, holding light dumbbells under your chest, soft elbows. Move: Raise your arms out to the sides until they are level with your torso, squeezing your shoulder blades, then lower slowly. Watch for: Shrugging and swinging. Tip: Use very light weights. A strong upper back helps your posture and protects your shoulders for bench pressing.

Pull-Up.cue: Start from a dead hang and pull the chest to the bar. Use a pull-up bar when one is available.
Pull-Up.howTo: Setup: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip a little wider than your shoulders, shoulders pulled down. Move: Drive your elbows down to your ribs until your chin passes the bar, then lower fully. Watch for: Kipping and half reps. Tip: Use a band, an assisted machine, or slow negatives (jump up, lower for 5 seconds) to build up.

Chin-Up.cue: Palms facing you, chin over the bar. Use a pull-up bar when one is available.
Chin-Up.howTo: Setup: Hang from a bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip. Pull your shoulder blades down. Move: Pull your chest toward the bar until your chin clears it, then lower all the way down. Watch for: Half reps or kicking. Tip: Usually easier than a pull-up because the biceps help. Use a band or negatives (lower for 5 seconds) to build up.

Lat Pulldown.cue: Pull the elbows to the ribs.
Lat Pulldown.howTo: Setup: Sit with thighs under the pad, grab the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width. Move: Pull the bar to your upper chest, driving your elbows down, then let it rise with control. Watch for: Leaning back and pulling behind your neck. Tip: Think of it as the pull-up for beginners.

Straight-Arm Pulldown.cue: Keep the arms long and sweep down.
Straight-Arm Pulldown.howTo: Setup: Stand facing a high cable with a straight bar, arms straight, hinged slightly. Move: Sweep the bar down to your thighs with straight arms, squeezing your lats, then return slowly. Watch for: Bending the elbows. Tip: Feel it in your back, not your arms.

Barbell Curl.cue: Elbows at the sides and no swinging.
Barbell Curl.howTo: Setup: Stand tall holding a bar with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width, elbows pinned at your sides. Move: Curl the bar up to shoulder height without letting your elbows drift forward, squeeze at the top, then lower for about 3 seconds. Watch for: Swinging your hips or leaning back to get the weight up. Tip: If you have to cheat to finish, the weight is too heavy. Lighter and slower builds more.

Hammer Curl.cue: Thumbs up and control the lowering.
Hammer Curl.howTo: Setup: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides with palms facing your thighs. Move: Curl the weights up with thumbs pointing to the ceiling, keeping your wrists straight, then lower slowly. Watch for: Swinging your torso or letting your elbows drift forward. Tip: This hits the forearms and the muscle under your biceps, which makes your arms look thicker. Alternate arms if it helps you stay strict.

Incline Curl.cue: Arms hang straight down and stretch the biceps.
Incline Curl.howTo: Setup: Sit back on a bench set at about 45 to 60 degrees, with your arms hanging straight down and palms forward. Move: Curl the dumbbells up without moving your upper arms, then lower all the way down to a full stretch. Watch for: Elbows drifting forward and half reps. Tip: The stretched position makes this tougher than it looks, so start much lighter than a standing curl.

Cable Curl.cue: Constant tension and a slow lowering phase.
Cable Curl.howTo: Setup: Face a low cable with a straight or EZ bar, elbows at your sides, feet staggered for balance. Move: Curl the handle up to your shoulders and lower slowly. Watch for: Leaning back or letting your elbows move. Tip: The cable keeps tension on your biceps through the whole rep, which dumbbells do not. A good finishing exercise.

Triceps Pushdown.howTo: Setup: Stand facing a high cable, grip the bar or rope, and pin your elbows to your sides. Move: Push down until your arms are straight, squeeze, then let the handle rise until your forearms are just past parallel. Watch for: Flaring your elbows or leaning over the weight. Tip: Only your forearms should move. If your shoulders move, lighten the load.

Skull Crusher.cue: Lower to the forehead and keep the elbows still.
Skull Crusher.howTo: Setup: Lie on a bench holding a bar or dumbbells over your chest with straight arms. Move: Bend only at the elbows to lower the weight toward your forehead or just behind your head, then extend. Watch for: Elbows flaring wide or the weight drifting toward your face. Tip: Lowering slightly behind your head protects your elbows. Use a spotter or light weights to start.

Overhead Triceps Extension.cue: Elbows close to the ears and a deep stretch.
Overhead Triceps Extension.howTo: Setup: Stand or sit holding one dumbbell overhead with both hands, elbows pointing forward and close to your ears. Move: Lower the weight behind your head by bending your elbows, then extend back up. Watch for: Arching your low back or flaring your elbows. Tip: The overhead position stretches the long head of the triceps, which is the biggest part. Brace your abs and keep the weight light.

Plank.cue: Ribs down and squeeze the glutes.
Plank.howTo: Setup: Forearms on the floor, elbows under shoulders, body in a straight line from head to heels. Move: Squeeze glutes and abs, breathe steadily, and hold for time. Watch for: Sagging hips or piking up. Tip: Quality beats time; stop when form drops. Do it from your knees to start.

Ab Wheel.cue: Roll out only as far as you can keep the lower back flat.
Ab Wheel.howTo: Setup: Kneel holding the wheel under your shoulders, ribs down, glutes tight. Move: Roll forward slowly as far as you can keep your back flat, then pull back using your abs. Watch for: Low back sagging. Tip: Roll against a wall to limit the range at first.

Pallof Press.cue: Resist rotation and keep the hips square.
Pallof Press.howTo: Setup: Stand sideways to a cable or anchored band at chest height, hands together at your chest, feet shoulder-width. Move: Press your hands straight out, resisting the pull to rotate, hold for a second or two, then bring them back. Watch for: Twisting toward the anchor or leaning away. Tip: It looks easy but trains the part of your core that protects your spine. Step farther from the anchor to make it harder.

Hanging Knee Raise.cue: Curl the pelvis up and avoid swinging.
Hanging Knee Raise.howTo: Setup: Hang from a bar with straight arms and shoulders pulled slightly down. Move: Curl your knees up toward your chest by tucking your pelvis, then lower slowly. Watch for: Swinging and using momentum. Tip: Think of lifting your hips up, not just your knees. Use a captain's chair if hanging is hard on your grip.

Dead Bug.cue: Press the lower back into the floor.
Dead Bug.howTo: Setup: Lie on your back with your arms pointing to the ceiling and your knees bent over your hips. Press your low back gently into the floor. Move: Slowly lower your opposite arm and leg toward the floor, keeping your back flat, then return and switch. Watch for: Your low back arching. Tip: Exhale as you extend. Slow beats fast. If your back arches, shorten the range.

Bird Dog.cue: Reach long and keep the hips level.
Bird Dog.howTo: Setup: Get on your hands and knees with a flat back, hands under shoulders, knees under hips. Move: Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until they are level with your torso, hold a moment, then return and switch. Watch for: Hips rotating or low back sagging. Tip: Pretend a cup of water is on your back. Move slowly and squeeze your glute.

Hollow Hold.cue: Lower back stays on the floor.
Hollow Hold.howTo: Setup: Lie on your back with your low back pressed to the floor and arms overhead. Move: Lift your shoulders and straight legs a few inches off the floor and hold, breathing steadily. Watch for: Your low back lifting. Tip: Bend your knees or keep your arms by your sides to make it easier.

Russian Twist.cue: Rotate through the ribs, not just the arms.
Russian Twist.howTo: Setup: Sit leaning back with knees bent, feet down (or raised for harder). Move: Rotate your torso to tap the floor beside each hip, alternating sides. Watch for: Rounding your back or only moving your arms. Tip: Rotate from the ribs. Hold a light weight only once the bodyweight version is smooth.

Cable Crunch.cue: Curl the ribs to the hips.
Cable Crunch.howTo: Setup: Kneel at a high cable, holding the rope beside your head. Move: Curl your ribs toward your hips, rounding your spine, then return slowly. Watch for: Sitting back on your heels or pulling with your arms. Tip: Think of crunching your ribs toward your pelvis.

Side Plank.cue: Stack the feet and lift the hips.
Side Plank.howTo: Setup: Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder and legs stacked. Move: Lift your hips to form a straight line from head to feet and hold, breathing steadily. Watch for: Hips sagging or rotating. Tip: Bend your knees to make it easier. Great for the sides of your core and hips.

Farmer Carry.cue: Walk tall with short quick steps.
Farmer Carry.howTo: Setup: Pick up a heavy weight in each hand by hinging at the hips, then stand tall with shoulders back and down. Move: Walk with short, quick steps, keeping your ribs stacked over your hips and your eyes forward. Put the weights down with a hinge, not a rounded back. Watch for: Leaning to one side or shrugging. Tip: The simplest full-body exercise there is. If your grip fails first, use straps sparingly and aim for longer distances over time.

Suitcase Carry.cue: Stay upright and do not lean into the weight.
Suitcase Carry.howTo: Setup: Pick up one heavy weight in one hand and stand tall. Move: Walk without tilting toward the weight, keeping your shoulders level and your abs braced. Switch hands halfway. Watch for: Leaning or letting your shoulder hike. Tip: This is core training disguised as walking. The side opposite the weight works hardest to keep you upright.

Overhead Carry.cue: Biceps by the ear and ribs down.
Overhead Carry.howTo: Setup: Press a light to moderate weight overhead with a locked elbow, ribs down, glutes squeezed. Move: Walk with small steps, keeping the weight stacked over your shoulder. Watch for: Arching your low back or letting the arm drift forward. Tip: Start light. It builds shoulder stability and teaches you to keep your ribs down.

Sled Push.cue: Low hips, drive with long steps.
Sled Push.howTo: Setup: Place your hands on the high posts and lean forward so your body is at a 45-degree angle. Move: Drive with your legs in strong, steady steps, keeping your back flat and arms straight. Watch for: A rounded back or short, choppy steps. Tip: Low impact and hard on the legs. Start with a light load and go for distance.

Bear Crawl.cue: Knees hover one inch off the floor.

Bear Crawl.howTo: Setup: Get on your hands and knees, then lift your knees an inch off the floor. Move: Crawl forward with opposite hand and foot, keeping your back flat and hips low. Watch for: Hips rising. Tip: Keep steps small and slow.

Air Bike Sprint.cue: Drive with legs and arms together.
Air Bike Sprint.howTo: Setup: Adjust the seat so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke. Grip the handles. Move: Push and pull the handles while pedaling hard for the set time, then rest. Watch for: Starting too fast and burning out. Tip: Pace the first interval. It should feel hard but repeatable. The harder you push, the more resistance you get.

Rowing Machine.howTo: Setup: Strap your feet in, grab the handle with a loose grip, and sit tall with shins vertical. Move: Push with your legs first, then lean back slightly, then pull the handle to your ribs. Reverse the order to return: arms, body, legs. Watch for: Pulling with your arms first or hunching. Tip: Legs do about 60 percent of the work. Keep a steady, smooth rhythm.

SkiErg.cue: Hinge and pull the handles down with the lats.
SkiErg.howTo: Setup: Stand facing the machine with your feet shoulder-width, handles overhead. Move: Pull the handles down toward your hips while hinging at the hips and bending your knees, then return. Watch for: Only using your arms. Tip: Think of it as a standing full-body pull. Smooth rhythm beats power.

Treadmill Run.cue: Stay relaxed and breathe in rhythm.
Treadmill Run.howTo: Setup: Start with a walking warm-up for a couple of minutes. Move: Run at a pace where you can breathe steadily, taking light, quick steps. Watch for: Overstriding and gripping the rails. Tip: Build up gradually. A 1 percent incline roughly matches outdoor running.

Jump Rope.howTo: Setup: Hold the handles at hip height with the rope behind your heels. Move: Jump a couple of inches off the floor, turning the rope with your wrists, landing softly on the balls of your feet. Watch for: Jumping too high or turning with the arms. Tip: Start with 20 to 30 second rounds. No rope? Mime it.

Burpee.cue: Chest to the floor, jump, repeat.
Burpee.howTo: Setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width. Move: Squat down, put your hands on the floor, jump or step your feet back to a plank, lower your chest to the floor, press up, bring your feet in, and jump up. Watch for: Sagging hips and a rounded back. Tip: Step instead of jump to make it easier. Move at a pace you can sustain.

Mountain Climber.howTo: Setup: High plank with hands under shoulders. Move: Drive one knee toward your chest, then switch quickly, keeping your hips low and back flat. Watch for: Hips bouncing high. Tip: Slow it down to make it harder on your core.

Thruster.cue: Squat to a press in one motion.
Thruster.howTo: Setup: Hold dumbbells at your shoulders, feet shoulder-width. Move: Squat down, then drive up and press the weights overhead in one smooth motion, lowering them back to your shoulders as you descend. Watch for: Pressing before your legs finish. Tip: Light weights. The power comes from your legs.

Dumbbell Complex.cue: Move from one lift to the next without setting the weight down.
Dumbbell Complex.howTo: Setup: Choose light dumbbells. Move: Without putting them down, do a set number of rows, cleans, squats, and presses in sequence. Watch for: Rushing. Tip: Pick the weight of your weakest move. A great way to build conditioning.

Dumbbell Clean and Press.cue: Pull the weight to the shoulders and press overhead.
Dumbbell Clean and Press.howTo: Setup: Stand over dumbbells on the floor, hinge with a flat back. Move: Pull the weights to your shoulders, then press them overhead. Lower them to your shoulders, then to the floor. Watch for: Curling the weights. Tip: Use your hips to power the pull.

Shuttle Run.cue: Touch the line each time and stay low on the turn.
Shuttle Run.howTo: Setup: Mark two lines about 10 yards apart. Move: Sprint to one line, touch it, turn, and sprint back. Watch for: Slipping. Tip: Lower your hips and plant your foot to turn.

Zone 2 Cardio.cue: Breathe through the nose and keep it conversational.
Zone 2 Cardio.howTo: Setup: Choose any steady activity you enjoy: walking, cycling, rowing, or jogging. Move: Keep a pace where you can speak in full sentences but could not sing. Watch for: Going too hard. Tip: This should feel easy. It builds your aerobic base, helps recovery, and supports heart health.

Rest Day.cue: Sleep well, hydrate and eat enough protein. An easy walk is optional.
Rest Day.howTo: Rest is when your body actually gets stronger. Aim for 7 to 9 hours of sleep, eat enough protein (a palm-sized portion at each meal), drink water, and take an easy walk if you feel like it. Skipping a hard session today protects tomorrow's.

Sprawl.cue: Hips down fast and pop back up.
Sprawl.howTo: Setup: Stand tall. Move: Drop your hips, kick your feet back to a plank, then pop back up. Watch for: Sagging hips. Tip: A burpee without the push-up.

Shadow Boxing Rounds.cue: Stay light on the feet and keep the hands up.
Shadow Boxing Rounds.howTo: Setup: Stand with feet staggered, hands up. Move: Throw punches in combinations while moving around, staying relaxed. Watch for: Locking out your elbows. Tip: Keep your breathing steady and your shoulders loose.

Medicine Ball Slam.howTo: Setup: Hold a ball overhead. Move: Slam it into the floor as hard as you can, catch it on the bounce. Watch for: Rounding your back. Tip: Use a non-bouncing ball. Power from your hips and abs.

Dumbbell Woodchop.howTo: Setup: Hold a dumbbell with both hands at your hip. Move: Swing it diagonally up and across your body to the opposite shoulder, pivoting your feet. Watch for: Arm-only movement. Tip: Rotate from your hips.

Turkish Get-Up.cue: Eyes on the weight and move one step at a time.
Turkish Get-Up.howTo: Setup: Lie on your back holding a weight straight up over your shoulder. Move: Stand up in steps (roll to elbow, hand, bridge, sweep your leg, kneel, stand), then reverse. Watch for: Rushing. Tip: Practice with no weight, or a shoe on your fist. Keep your eyes on the weight.

Dumbbell Snatch.cue: Pull high and punch through at the top.
Dumbbell Snatch.howTo: Setup: Stand over a dumbbell between your feet, hinge with a flat back. Move: Pull it overhead in one motion, driving with your hips, then lower it back down. Watch for: Curling the weight. Tip: Light dumbbell, hip power.

Power Clean.cue: Jump, shrug, and catch with elbows fast.
Power Clean.howTo: Setup: Barbell on the floor, feet hip-width, flat back. Move: Pull explosively and catch the bar at your shoulders, then lower. Watch for: Early arm bend. Tip: Technical. Learn with a coach.

Jump Squat.howTo: Setup: Squat stance. Move: Squat and jump straight up, landing softly. Watch for: Stiff landings. Tip: Keep jumps modest and land quietly.

Box Jump.howTo: Setup: Stand in front of a box with feet hip-width. Move: Swing your arms and jump onto the box, landing softly with bent knees. Stand tall, then step down. Watch for: Jumping off the box. Tip: Choose a lower box than you think you need.

Broad Jump.cue: Swing the arms and stick the landing.
Broad Jump.howTo: Setup: Stand with feet hip-width. Move: Swing your arms and jump forward as far as you can, landing softly. Watch for: Stiff landings. Tip: Stick each landing.

Plyometric Push-Up.cue: Push the floor away hard and land softly.
Plyometric Push-Up.howTo: Setup: Strong plank with hands under your shoulders. Move: Lower your chest, then push the floor away hard enough that your hands leave it, and land with soft elbows into the next rep. Watch for: Collapsing on landing or sagging hips. Tip: This is a power exercise, so do only the reps you can do crisply and stop when they slow down. Practice on an elevated surface first.

Lateral Bound.cue: Push off one foot and stick the landing.
Lateral Bound.howTo: Setup: Stand on one leg. Move: Jump sideways and land on the other leg, holding the landing. Watch for: Wobbly knees. Tip: Short bounds first.

Skater Jump.cue: Jump sideways and land on one foot.
Skater Jump.howTo: Setup: Stand on one leg. Move: Bound side to side, landing softly. Watch for: Knee collapse. Tip: Keep the range small to start.

Glute Bridge.cue: Drive through the heels and squeeze at the top.
Glute Bridge.howTo: Setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width. Move: Press through your heels to lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees. Squeeze your glutes for a second, then lower. Watch for: Arching the low back instead of using the glutes. Tip: A classic warm-up to wake up your glutes.

90/90 Hip Switch.howTo: Setup: Sit on the floor with both knees bent at 90 degrees and both legs dropped to one side, torso tall. Move: Rotate your knees over to the other side, using your hands for balance if needed, and sit tall again. Watch for: Rounding your back or forcing the knees down. Tip: Move slowly. If it is too tight, sit on a folded towel. It opens up the hips for squats.

Hip Flexor Stretch.cue: Tuck the pelvis and squeeze the rear glute.
Hip Flexor Stretch.howTo: Setup: Kneel on one knee with the other foot forward, on a pad. Tuck your pelvis and squeeze the glute of the back leg. Move: Shift your hips forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the back hip. Hold 30 seconds, breathing slowly. Watch for: Arching your low back. Tip: The glute squeeze is what makes the stretch work. Great after sitting all day.

Cat-Cow.cue: Move the whole spine with each breath.
Cat-Cow.howTo: Setup: Get on your hands and knees, hands under shoulders, knees under hips. Move: Inhale and let your belly drop as you look up (cow), exhale and round your spine toward the ceiling (cat). Flow with your breath. Watch for: Rushing. Tip: Gently warms up the spine. Do 8 to 10 slow cycles.

Thoracic Rotation.cue: Follow the hand with the eyes.
Thoracic Rotation.howTo: Setup: On hands and knees, place one hand behind your head. Move: Rotate that elbow down toward the opposite wrist, then open up toward the ceiling, following with your eyes. Watch for: Your hips shifting. Tip: Opens up your upper back for overhead lifts and better posture.

Child's Pose.howTo: Setup: Kneel, sit back on your heels, and reach your arms forward with your forehead on the floor. Move: Breathe slowly into your back and hold 30 to 60 seconds. Watch for: Knee pain. Tip: Place a pillow between your calves and thighs if your knees are tight.

Deep Squat Hold.howTo: Setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width and toes turned out. Move: Sink into the deepest comfortable squat, elbows pressing the knees out, chest tall, and hold. Watch for: Heels lifting. Tip: Hold on to a post for balance or sit on a low box. Great for hips and ankles.

Wall Slide.cue: Keep the ribs down and forearms on the wall.
Wall Slide.howTo: Setup: Stand with your back, head, and arms flat against a wall, elbows bent at 90 degrees. Move: Slide your arms up the wall, keeping contact, then back down. Watch for: Your back arching off the wall. Tip: Great for shoulder health and posture.

Thread the Needle.howTo: Setup: On hands and knees. Move: Slide one arm under your chest along the floor and rest your shoulder and head down, then return. Watch for: Forcing it. Tip: Breathe slowly; it opens up the upper back.

Dead Hang.cue: Relax the shoulders and hang long.
Dead Hang.howTo: Setup: Grip a bar and hang with arms straight. Move: Hold for time, breathing steadily, shoulders slightly engaged. Watch for: Letting shoulders shrug up. Tip: Builds grip and stretches your lats. Stand on a box or keep a foot on a chair if full hangs are tough.

Doorway Pec Stretch.cue: Elbow at shoulder height and lean through.
Doorway Pec Stretch.howTo: Setup: Stand in a doorway with your forearm on the frame and elbow at 90 degrees. Move: Step through slightly until you feel a stretch across your chest. Hold 30 seconds. Watch for: Shrugging your shoulder. Tip: Great after a day of pressing or desk work.

World's Greatest Stretch.howTo: Setup: Step into a long lunge, hands on the floor inside your front foot. Move: Rotate your torso and reach the inside arm to the ceiling, then drop back and switch. Watch for: Rushing. Tip: It loosens hips, back, and shoulders in a single move.

Cossack Squat.cue: Sit into one hip and keep the other leg long.
Cossack Squat.howTo: Setup: Stand with a wide stance. Move: Shift your weight onto one leg, sit into a deep side squat while the other leg stays straight with the toes up, then switch. Watch for: Heel lifting. Tip: Hold a post for support and go only as deep as comfortable.

Hamstring Stretch.cue: Keep the leg straight and relax the neck.
Hamstring Stretch.howTo: Setup: Lie on your back with a strap or towel around one foot, or sit tall with one leg extended. Move: Straighten the leg and gently pull toward you until you feel the stretch behind the thigh. Hold 30 seconds. Watch for: Bouncing. Tip: Keep your back flat. Breathe slowly.

Couch Stretch.cue: Back knee near the wall and ribs down.
Couch Stretch.howTo: Setup: Kneel with one foot up against a wall or couch behind you. Move: Squeeze your glute and lean upright until you feel the front of your thigh stretch. Watch for: Arching your low back. Tip: Intense. Start with a shorter time and increase.

Pigeon Stretch.howTo: Setup: From hands and knees, bring one knee forward behind your wrist and slide the other leg back. Move: Lower your hips and fold forward over your front leg. Watch for: Knee pain. Tip: Put a cushion under your hip. Skip it if your knees complain and use the figure-four stretch.

Ankle Rock.cue: Drive the knee over the toes with the heel down.
Ankle Rock.howTo: Setup: Half-kneel with the front foot flat. Move: Drive the front knee forward over your toes without lifting your heel, then rock back. Watch for: Heel lifting. Tip: Improves the ankle mobility you need for squats.

Zercher Squat.cue: Bar in the elbow crease, chest tall, sit between the hips.
Zercher Squat.howTo: Setup: Hold the bar in the crooks of your elbows against your stomach (pad it with a towel). Feet shoulder-width. Move: Sit between your hips, keeping your elbows pointing forward and chest tall, then stand. Watch for: The bar rolling out of the elbows or the chest collapsing. Tip: Uncomfortable at first. Start light and keep sets short.

Leg Extension.cue: Pause at the top and lower under control.
Leg Extension.howTo: Setup: Sit with your back flat and the pad just above your ankles; line your knee up with the machine pivot. Move: Straighten your knees fully, squeeze the quads for a second, then lower slowly. Watch for: Swinging the weight up with momentum. Tip: Choose a weight you can lift smoothly for all reps. Skip it if it bothers your knees and use the wall sit or step-up instead.

Curtsy Lunge.cue: Step back and across, keep the front knee over the foot.
Curtsy Lunge.howTo: Setup: Stand tall, feet hip-width. Move: Step one leg diagonally behind and across the other as if curtsying, lowering your back knee toward the floor, then drive through the front heel to return. Watch for: The front knee collapsing inward or the torso twisting. Tip: Works the outer glute. Hold a wall if balance is wobbly.

Pistol Squat.cue: Sit to a box on one leg and keep the heel down.
Pistol Squat.howTo: Setup: Stand in front of a box or chair, one foot lifted. Move: Sit back to the box on one leg, touching lightly, then stand without pushing from the free leg. Watch for: Heel lifting or knee caving in. Tip: A very advanced move. Use a high box and hold a pole for help and work down gradually.

Sissy Squat.cue: Lean back, knees forward, hips locked in line.
Sissy Squat.howTo: Setup: Hold a post or rack for balance. Rise onto your toes. Move: Lean back with hips locked in line and let your knees travel forward as you lower, then come back up. Watch for: Bending at the hips. Tip: This hits the front of the thigh and is tough on knees. Start with a small range.

Forward Lunge.cue: Step long, drop the back knee, push back to standing.
Forward Lunge.howTo: Setup: Stand tall, feet hip-width. Move: Step forward into a long stance, lower your back knee toward the floor, then push through the front foot back to standing. Watch for: A short step that puts the knee far over the toes, and leaning forward. Tip: Reverse lunges are easier on the knees, so use those first if this bothers you.

Heel-Elevated Squat.cue: Heels on a plate, knees travel forward, torso upright.
Heel-Elevated Squat.howTo: Setup: Put your heels on a small plate or wedge about an inch or two high. Move: Squat down with your knees traveling forward and torso upright, then stand. The lift makes deeper squats easier. Watch for: Falling forward onto your toes. Tip: A good way to find depth if your ankles are stiff.

Lateral Step-Up.cue: Stand beside the box, step up with the near leg and lower slowly.
Lateral Step-Up.howTo: Setup: Stand sideways next to a low box. Move: Place the near foot on the box and stand up through that leg without pushing off the floor foot, then lower slowly. Watch for: Leaning sideways or using the bottom foot. Tip: Lower the step if you cannot control the way down.

Wall Sit.cue: Thighs parallel, back flat on the wall.
Wall Sit.howTo: Setup: Put your back flat on a wall and slide down until your thighs are parallel to the floor, knees over ankles. Move: Hold, breathing steadily, with your hands off your thighs. Watch for: Sliding up as it burns. Tip: Start with 20 to 30 seconds and add time each week.

Sumo Squat.cue: Wide stance, toes out, knees track over the toes.
Sumo Squat.howTo: Setup: Stand with a wide stance, toes turned out about 45 degrees, hold a weight between your legs if you have one. Move: Sit straight down keeping your knees tracking over your toes, then squeeze your glutes and inner thighs to stand. Watch for: Knees caving in. Tip: A nice way to work the inner thighs and glutes.

Stiff-Leg Deadlift.cue: Knees nearly straight, hinge until the hamstrings stretch.
Stiff-Leg Deadlift.howTo: Setup: Stand tall, weight in front of your thighs, knees nearly straight (but not locked). Move: Hinge from the hips until you feel a strong hamstring stretch, then stand by squeezing your glutes. Watch for: Rounding your back to reach lower. Tip: Go only as low as your back stays flat.

Rack Pull.cue: Bar starts at the knee, lock out with the glutes.
Rack Pull.howTo: Setup: Set the bar on a rack at knee height. Grip just outside your legs, chest up, back flat. Move: Push the floor away and stand tall, squeezing the glutes at the top. Lower under control. Watch for: Leaning back at the top. Tip: A shorter version of the deadlift; ideal for learning the lockout.

Single-Leg Hip Thrust.cue: Ribs down, drive through the heel, squeeze at the top.
Single-Leg Hip Thrust.howTo: Setup: Upper back against a bench, one foot flat, the other leg lifted with the knee bent. Move: Drive through the heel to raise your hips until your torso is level, squeeze the glute, and lower. Watch for: Hips twisting open and low back arching. Tip: Do the two-leg version until you can control it.

Cable Pull-Through.cue: Hinge back, then snap the hips forward.
Cable Pull-Through.howTo: Setup: Face away from a low cable with the rope between your legs, stepping a few feet forward. Move: Hinge your hips back, then snap them forward and squeeze your glutes to stand. Arms stay long. Watch for: Squatting instead of hinging. Tip: An easy way to practice the hip hinge.

Nordic Hamstring Curl.cue: Lower slowly with a straight hip line and catch yourself at the floor.
Nordic Hamstring Curl.howTo: Setup: Kneel on a pad with your feet anchored under something sturdy or held by a partner. Move: Keeping your body straight from the knees to the head, lower as slowly as you can, catch yourself with your hands, and push back up. Watch for: Bending at the hips. Tip: Very intense. Even 2 to 3 reps per set is a great start.

Slider Hamstring Curl.cue: Bridge up, slide out slowly, curl back.
Slider Hamstring Curl.howTo: Setup: Lie on your back with your heels on sliders (or towels on a smooth floor) and hips lifted in a bridge. Move: Slide your feet out slowly, then pull them back in using your hamstrings, keeping your hips up. Watch for: Hips sagging. Tip: Shorten the distance if it is too hard.

Seated Calf Raise.cue: Bent knees target the soleus. Pause at the top.
Seated Calf Raise.howTo: Setup: Sit with the pad on your knees and balls of your feet on the platform. Move: Lower your heels for a deep stretch, then press all the way up and pause. Watch for: Bouncing at the bottom. Tip: The bent knee shifts the work to the deeper calf muscle, so you need both this and the standing calf raise.

Banded Lateral Walk.cue: Stay in a quarter squat and keep tension on the band.
Banded Lateral Walk.howTo: Setup: Put a mini band around your thighs or ankles and sink into a quarter squat. Move: Take small steps sideways, keeping your toes forward and tension on the band, then return. Watch for: Knees caving in and leaning. Tip: You should feel it in the sides of your hips.

Reverse Hyperextension.cue: Swing the legs up with control and avoid over-arching.
Reverse Hyperextension.howTo: Setup: Lie face down with your hips at the edge of a bench or machine and legs hanging. Move: Raise your legs until they line up with your body, squeeze the glutes, and lower with control. Watch for: Swinging and over-arching the low back. Tip: Floor version works too; lift both legs and pause.

Decline Bench Press.cue: Slight decline, bar to the lower chest.
Decline Bench Press.howTo: Setup: Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured and the bar over your lower chest. Grip a little wider than your shoulders. Move: Lower the bar to your lower chest, then press up. Watch for: Heavy weights, because this angle is awkward to bail from. Tip: Always use a spotter. If you do not have a decline bench, dips or a regular bench with a slow lowering phase do a similar job.

Machine Chest Press.cue: Set the handles at mid-chest and press without shrugging.
Machine Chest Press.howTo: Setup: Adjust the seat so the handles are level with the middle of your chest. Sit with your back flat on the pad and feet planted. Move: Press the handles forward until your arms are nearly straight, then return slowly until your hands are at chest level. Watch for: Shrugging your shoulders and locking your elbows hard. Tip: A very safe first chest exercise because the machine guides the path. Start light and focus on a smooth, controlled tempo.

Pike Push-Up.cue: Hips high, head between the arms, press the crown forward.
Pike Push-Up.howTo: Setup: Start in a downward-dog shape, hips high, hands shoulder-width, feet a bit wider than hips. Move: Bend your elbows to lower the top of your head toward the floor between your hands, then press back up. Watch for: Flaring elbows or sinking into a regular push-up. Tip: A bodyweight shoulder press. Raise your hands on a step to make it easier.

Diamond Push-Up.cue: Hands form a diamond under the chest, elbows close.
Diamond Push-Up.howTo: Setup: Place your hands together under your chest, thumbs and index fingers forming a diamond. Body in a straight line. Move: Lower your chest toward your hands with elbows close to your ribs, then press up. Watch for: Elbows flaring or hips sagging. Tip: This targets the triceps. If your wrists complain, spread your hands a little or do them from your knees.

Cable Crossover.cue: Soft elbows, bring the hands together in an arc.
Cable Crossover.howTo: Setup: Stand between high cables, one foot forward, torso leaning slightly. Move: With soft elbows, bring your hands together in front of you in a wide arc, squeeze, and return slowly. Watch for: Using body swing. Tip: Keep the weight light enough that you feel the chest and not the shoulders.

Pec Deck Fly.cue: Squeeze the chest and keep the shoulders back.
Pec Deck Fly.howTo: Setup: Sit with your back flat against the pad and handles at chest height. Move: Squeeze your arms together in front of you, pause, and open with control. Watch for: Shrugging or letting the weight stack slam. Tip: Do not let your elbows travel behind your body.

Z Press.cue: Sit on the floor with legs straight and do not lean back.
Z Press.howTo: Setup: Sit on the floor with your legs straight in front of you, holding the weights or bar at your shoulders. Move: Press overhead while keeping your torso upright, then lower to your shoulders. Watch for: Leaning back or rounding your low back. Tip: Brutally honest for your core and mobility, so go lighter than a standing press. Sit on a folded mat if your hamstrings are tight.

Front Raise.cue: Raise to eye level with no swing.
Front Raise.howTo: Setup: Stand holding light dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms facing you, a soft bend in your elbows. Move: Raise your arms straight in front to shoulder height, pause, then lower slowly. Watch for: Swinging your body or going above shoulder height. Tip: Your front shoulders already work in pressing, so keep this light and controlled.

Standing Dumbbell Press.cue: Squeeze the glutes and press straight overhead without leaning.
Standing Dumbbell Press.howTo: Setup: Stand with feet hip-width, dumbbells at your shoulders, palms facing forward or in. Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs. Move: Press the weights straight up until your arms are straight beside your ears, then lower to your shoulders. Watch for: Leaning back and arching the low back. Tip: If you start to lean, the weight is too heavy. Squeezing your glutes keeps your ribs down and your lower back safe.

Cable Lateral Raise.cue: Lead with the elbow and stop at shoulder height.
Cable Lateral Raise.howTo: Setup: Stand sideways to a low cable, handle in the far hand. Move: Raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height with a soft elbow, then lower slowly. Watch for: Leaning away. Tip: Cables keep tension on the muscle at the bottom, which dumbbells do not.

Triceps Kickback.cue: Upper arm pinned to the torso, extend fully.
Triceps Kickback.howTo: Setup: Hinge forward with a flat back, holding a dumbbell with your upper arm parallel to the floor and elbow bent. Move: Straighten your elbow to extend your arm behind you, squeeze, then return. Watch for: Swinging the weight. Tip: Light weight and a pause at the top works much better than heavy swinging.

JM Press.cue: Elbows in, lower to the upper chest and press back.
JM Press.howTo: Setup: Lie on a bench holding a bar or dumbbells over your chest with a close grip. Move: Bend only at the elbows to lower the weight toward your chin or upper chest, then extend. It is half bench press, half skull crusher. Watch for: Elbows flaring wide. Tip: Use light weight and a spotter. It is easy to overload.

Inverted Row.cue: Body in a straight line, pull the chest to the bar.
Inverted Row.howTo: Setup: Lie under a sturdy bar or table, holding it with arms straight, body in a straight line, heels on the floor. Move: Pull your chest to the bar, squeeze your shoulder blades, then lower. Watch for: Sagging hips. Tip: Bend your knees to make it easier, or lower the bar to make it harder.

Meadows Row.cue: Stagger the stance, row to the hip and squeeze the lat.
Meadows Row.howTo: Setup: Stand sideways to a barbell anchored in a corner with one end loaded. Hinge forward with a flat back and grip the loaded end. Move: Row it to your hip with your elbow high, squeeze, and lower with control. Watch for: Standing up as you pull. Tip: Keep the weight moderate. A dumbbell row is a good substitute.

T-Bar Row.cue: Chest up, pull to the lower ribs.
T-Bar Row.howTo: Setup: Straddle the bar, hinge until your torso is at about 45 degrees, and grab the handle with a flat back. Move: Pull the handle to your chest, squeeze your shoulder blades together, and lower under control. Watch for: Jerking the weight or rounding your back. Tip: A chest pad makes this friendlier. It is a good moderate-weight back builder.

Single-Arm Cable Row.cue: Row to the hip and let the shoulder blade glide.
Single-Arm Cable Row.howTo: Setup: Face a low cable, feet planted, one hand on the handle, other arm free. Move: Pull the handle to your ribs with your elbow close, then return slowly without letting your shoulder roll forward. Watch for: Twisting your torso. Tip: Rotate slightly as you pull to feel the lat. Do both sides evenly.

Neutral-Grip Pull-Up.cue: Palms facing, chest to the bar.
Neutral-Grip Pull-Up.howTo: Setup: Hang from parallel handles with palms facing each other. Move: Pull until your chin is above the handles, then lower fully. Watch for: Swinging. Tip: Kind to the shoulders and elbows. A good place to start.

Wide-Grip Pull-Up.cue: Hands wider than the shoulders, drive the elbows to the ribs.
Wide-Grip Pull-Up.howTo: Setup: Hang with a grip well wider than your shoulders. Move: Drive your elbows down toward your ribs until your chin clears the bar. Watch for: Reaching your chin forward. Tip: Harder than regular pull-ups, so expect fewer reps.

Scapular Pull-Up.cue: Hang with straight arms and pull the shoulder blades down.
Scapular Pull-Up.howTo: Setup: Hang from a bar with straight arms. Move: Without bending your elbows, pull your shoulder blades down and together so your body rises a couple of inches, then relax. Watch for: Bending your elbows. Tip: A great first step if you cannot yet do a full pull-up.

Dumbbell Pullover.cue: Reach back with the ribs down and pull with the lats.
Dumbbell Pullover.howTo: Setup: Lie across a bench with one dumbbell held in both hands above your chest. Move: Lower it back behind your head with a slight bend in the elbows until you feel a stretch, then pull it back over your chest. Watch for: Arching hard. Tip: Light weight; stop when the stretch is strong.

Band Pull-Apart.cue: Arms straight, pull the band apart at chest level and squeeze.
Band Pull-Apart.howTo: Setup: Hold a light resistance band at chest height with straight arms. Move: Pull the band apart until it touches your chest, squeeze your shoulder blades, then return slowly. Watch for: Shrugging. Tip: A quick posture fix that works anywhere, including at home.

Shrug.cue: Lift straight up, hold, lower slowly.
Shrug.howTo: Setup: Stand holding weights at your sides. Move: Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears, pause, then lower slowly. Watch for: Rolling your shoulders. Tip: Straight up and down, no rolling. Light to moderate weight with a pause at the top.

Preacher Curl.cue: Full range, stretch at the bottom without bouncing.
Preacher Curl.howTo: Setup: Sit with your upper arms flat on the angled pad and your armpits snug against the top. Move: Curl the weight up, then lower it slowly until your arms are nearly straight. Watch for: Dropping fast at the bottom, which can stress the elbow. Tip: Stop just short of full lockout and use a lighter weight than you think. The pad stops any cheating.

Concentration Curl.cue: Elbow on the inner thigh and curl without swinging.
Concentration Curl.howTo: Setup: Sit on a bench with your feet wide and rest the back of one upper arm against your inner thigh. Move: Curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder, squeeze for a beat, then lower slowly. Watch for: Swinging or using your shoulder. Tip: Slow and mindful. This is about feeling the muscle work, not lifting heavy.

Zottman Curl.cue: Curl palms up, rotate at the top, lower palms down.
Zottman Curl.howTo: Setup: Stand holding dumbbells with palms facing forward. Move: Curl up with palms forward, rotate your wrists so palms face down at the top, then lower slowly in that position. Rotate back at the bottom. Watch for: Going too heavy, which makes the lowering sloppy. Tip: Works your biceps going up and your forearms coming down.

Reverse Curl.cue: Overhand grip, elbows pinned, wrists straight.
Reverse Curl.howTo: Setup: Hold a bar or dumbbells with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width, elbows at your sides. Move: Curl up while keeping your wrists straight, then lower slowly. Watch for: Wrists bending back. Tip: Use a lighter weight than a normal curl. It builds forearm strength you will notice in pull-ups and carries.

Wrist Curl.cue: Forearms on the thighs, roll the weight to the fingertips and curl up.
Wrist Curl.howTo: Setup: Sit and rest your forearms on your thighs or a bench, palms up, wrists hanging past the edge, holding a light weight. Move: Curl your wrists up, then lower until you feel a stretch. Watch for: Using heavy weights and short range. Tip: Light weight, lots of reps. Grip strength helps nearly every other lift.

Hanging Leg Raise.cue: No swing, lift the legs to hip height or higher.
Hanging Leg Raise.howTo: Setup: Hang from a bar with straight arms. Move: Raise your straight legs to hip height or higher, then lower slowly without swinging. Watch for: Swinging or letting your back arch. Tip: Bend your knees to make it easier. Hanging also decompresses the spine.

Toes-to-Bar.cue: Pull the bar down with the lats and bring the toes to it.
Toes-to-Bar.howTo: Setup: Hang from a bar with a firm grip. Move: Raise your toes to touch the bar, then lower under control. Watch for: Wild kipping. Tip: Advanced. Work through hanging knee raises and leg raises first.

V-Up.cue: Reach the hands to the toes while lifting the legs.
V-Up.howTo: Setup: Lie flat with arms overhead and legs straight. Move: Raise your legs and torso together, reaching for your toes, then lower with control. Watch for: Using momentum. Tip: Tuck your knees to make it easier.

Bicycle Crunch.cue: Slow rotation, elbow to the opposite knee.
Bicycle Crunch.howTo: Setup: Lie on your back with your hands lightly by your head and knees raised. Move: Bring one elbow toward the opposite knee while extending the other leg, then switch in a pedaling motion. Watch for: Pulling on your neck. Tip: Go slow and rotate your ribcage, not just your elbows.

Sit-Up.cue: Feet anchored, curl up with control.
Sit-Up.howTo: Setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, arms crossed on your chest. Move: Curl up until your chest reaches your thighs, then lower with control. Watch for: Yanking on your neck or flinging your arms. Tip: Anchor your feet under a bar if they lift.

L-Sit.cue: Press down with straight legs parallel to the floor.
L-Sit.howTo: Setup: Sit with legs straight and hands flat beside your hips. Move: Press down, lift your hips and legs off the floor, and hold. Watch for: Shoulders shrugging. Tip: Start with bent knees or on parallettes.

Copenhagen Plank.cue: Top leg on a bench, hips stacked, lift the bottom leg.
Copenhagen Plank.howTo: Setup: Lie on your side with your top foot or knee resting on a bench and your elbow under your shoulder. Move: Lift your hips and bottom leg, hold a straight line. Watch for: Hips dropping. Tip: Advanced inner-thigh work. Rest your knee on the bench to start.

Landmine Rotation.cue: Turn through the hips and keep the arms long.
Landmine Rotation.howTo: Setup: Hold the end of a landmine bar with both hands at your chest, feet shoulder-width. Move: Rotate the end side to side by pivoting your feet and hips. Watch for: Arm-only movement. Tip: Keep your arms long and rotate from the trunk.

Reverse Crunch.cue: Curl the hips off the floor and do not swing.
Reverse Crunch.howTo: Setup: Lie on your back with knees bent over your hips. Move: Curl your hips off the floor toward your ribs, then lower slowly. Watch for: Swinging your legs. Tip: Lift only a few inches.

Flutter Kick.cue: Low back flat, small fast kicks.
Flutter Kick.howTo: Setup: Lie on your back with your low back flat and legs hovering. Move: Kick your legs in small alternating movements. Watch for: Your low back arching. Tip: Raise your legs higher if your back lifts.

Plank Shoulder Tap.cue: Feet wide, hips still, tap alternating shoulders.
Plank Shoulder Tap.howTo: Setup: High plank with feet wide. Move: Tap one shoulder with the opposite hand, keeping your hips still, then alternate. Watch for: Hips rocking. Tip: A wider stance makes it easier.

Lying Leg Raise.cue: Press the low back down and lower the legs slowly.
Lying Leg Raise.howTo: Setup: Lie on your back with legs straight and hands under your hips. Move: Raise your legs to vertical, then lower slowly. Watch for: Your back arching. Tip: Bend your knees if your back lifts.

Sled Pull.cue: Lean back, take small steps, drive through the quads.
Sled Pull.howTo: Setup: Attach straps or a rope to the sled. Face it or walk backwards. Move: Pull hand over hand, or walk backwards with the straps at your hips, keeping your chest tall. Watch for: Leaning back too far. Tip: Easy on the joints and great for the legs and back.

Kettlebell Clean.cue: Keep it close, drive the hips, catch softly.
Kettlebell Clean.howTo: Setup: Kettlebell on the floor between your feet. Move: Swing it back, then pull it to the rack position at your chest. Watch for: Banging your forearm. Tip: Keep it close to your body.

Kettlebell Snatch.cue: Hips drive it overhead and punch through at the top.
Kettlebell Snatch.howTo: Setup: Kettlebell between your feet. Move: Swing it up overhead in one motion. Watch for: Banging your wrist. Tip: Learn the swing first.

Hang Power Clean.cue: Slide the bar to the knee, jump, shrug, catch with the elbows up.
Hang Power Clean.howTo: Setup: Bar at the thighs, hinge slightly. Move: Pull and catch the bar at your shoulders. Watch for: Bending the arms too early. Tip: Start with a light bar.

Medicine Ball Chest Pass.cue: Drive from the chest, catch and reset.
Medicine Ball Chest Pass.howTo: Setup: Hold a ball at your chest. Move: Throw it forward hard against a wall. Watch for: Leaning. Tip: Step into it.

Medicine Ball Rotational Throw.cue: Load the back hip, rotate and release.
Medicine Ball Rotational Throw.howTo: Setup: Stand sideways to a wall. Move: Rotate and throw. Watch for: Arms only. Tip: Power from the hips.

Overhead Medicine Ball Throw.cue: Load slightly, extend the hips and throw.
Overhead Medicine Ball Throw.howTo: Setup: Hold the ball overhead. Move: Throw it forward. Watch for: Arching your back. Tip: Keep ribs down.

Tuck Jump.cue: Jump tall, pull the knees up and land softly.
Tuck Jump.howTo: Setup: Stand tall. Move: Jump and bring your knees toward your chest. Watch for: Hard landings. Tip: Go low.

Split Jump.cue: Land soft in a lunge and switch legs in the air.
Split Jump.howTo: Setup: Lunge position. Move: Jump and switch legs in the air. Watch for: Hard landings. Tip: Use a small jump.

Single-Leg Hop.cue: Hop in place or forward and stick the landing.
Single-Leg Hop.howTo: Setup: Stand on one leg. Move: Hop forward and stick the landing. Watch for: Wobbling. Tip: Slow down.

Bounding.cue: Exaggerated running strides, drive the knee up and push off hard.
Bounding.howTo: Setup: Stand tall. Move: Leap forward from one leg to the other. Watch for: Stiff landings. Tip: Start with small bounds.

High Knees.cue: Drive the knees to hip height and stay on the balls of the feet.
High Knees.howTo: Setup: Stand tall. Move: Run in place, driving your knees up to hip height with quick arms. Watch for: Leaning back. Tip: Stay light on your feet. Do march in place if you need low impact.

Jumping Jack.cue: Soft knees, arms overhead, land quietly.
Jumping Jack.howTo: Setup: Stand with feet together and arms at your sides. Move: Jump your feet out wide as your arms rise overhead, then jump back. Watch for: Heavy landings. Tip: For a low-impact version, step out to the side instead of jumping.

Battle Rope Wave.cue: Athletic stance, whip the ropes from the shoulders.
Battle Rope Wave.howTo: Setup: Hold the rope ends, feet shoulder-width, in a half squat. Move: Alternate raising and lowering your arms to create waves, keeping your core tight. Watch for: Rounded back. Tip: Keep it rhythmic. Small waves are fine.

Battle Rope Slam.cue: Raise overhead and slam down using the hips.
Battle Rope Slam.howTo: Setup: Hold the rope ends in a half squat. Move: Raise both arms overhead and slam the rope down hard, using your legs. Watch for: Using only your arms. Tip: Power from your hips.

Incline Treadmill Walk.cue: Keep the shoulders relaxed and do not hold the handrails.
Incline Treadmill Walk.howTo: Setup: Set the treadmill to an incline of 8 to 12 percent and a comfortable speed. Move: Walk with an upright posture without holding on. Watch for: Gripping the rails. Tip: A joint-friendly way to build cardio and glute strength.

Stationary Bike Ride.cue: Smooth cadence. Keep easy rides conversational.
Stationary Bike Ride.howTo: Setup: Adjust the seat to hip height so your knee has a slight bend at the bottom of each pedal stroke. Move: Pedal at a steady pace. Watch for: Hunching. Tip: Low impact; great for recovery days.

Hill Sprint.cue: Drive the knees, lean in, walk down for full recovery.
Hill Sprint.howTo: Setup: Find a moderate hill and warm up thoroughly. Move: Sprint up, then walk down to recover. Watch for: Overstriding and pushing too hard on your first sprint. Tip: Hills are gentler on hamstrings than flat sprints.

Weighted Ruck March.cue: Pack high and snug, walk tall at a steady pace.
Weighted Ruck March.howTo: Setup: Wear a pack with a modest weight (start with 10 to 15 pounds), straps snug and high on your back. Move: Walk at a brisk pace with a tall posture, taking natural strides. Watch for: Leaning forward or loads that strain your back. Tip: A simple way to build conditioning and back strength. Increase weight gradually.

Inchworm.cue: Walk the hands out to a plank and back with the legs straight.
Inchworm.howTo: Setup: Stand tall. Move: Hinge down, walk your hands out to a plank, then walk them back to your feet and stand. Watch for: Sagging in the plank. Tip: Keep legs as straight as comfortable.

Crab Walk.cue: Hips high, walk forward and back.
Crab Walk.howTo: Setup: Sit with your hands behind you and lift your hips. Move: Walk forward or backward on hands and feet. Watch for: Hips sagging. Tip: Works the shoulders, triceps, and glutes. Short distances at first.

Flat Sprint.cue: Tall posture, drive the arms, relax the face.
Flat Sprint.howTo: Setup: Clear a flat, safe space and warm up well. Move: Sprint at about 90 percent effort, then walk back to recover. Watch for: Tight hamstrings. Tip: Do not go all out on your first sprints. Build up.

Stair Climb.cue: Drive through the whole foot and stand tall.
Stair Climb.howTo: Setup: Find a staircase. Move: Climb at a steady pace, using your legs and driving through the whole foot. Watch for: Leaning and relying on the rail. Tip: Skip a step for more glute work.

Shoulder Pass-Through.cue: Wide grip, arms straight, go only as far as you can without pain.
Shoulder Pass-Through.howTo: Setup: Hold a stick, towel, or band with a wide grip. Move: Raise it overhead and then behind you with straight arms, then return. Watch for: Bending your elbows. Tip: Widen your grip until it is smooth.

Hip CARs.cue: Draw the biggest slow circle with the knee while the torso stays still.
Hip CARs.howTo: Setup: Stand holding a support, balancing on one leg. Move: Lift your knee up and out, then back in a big slow circle, keeping the rest of your body still. Watch for: Rocking. Tip: Slow, controlled, as large as you can make it.

Lizard Pose.cue: Both hands inside the front foot and sink the hips.
Lizard Pose.howTo: Setup: Step into a deep lunge with both hands inside the front foot. Move: Sink your hips toward the floor and breathe. Hold 30 seconds. Watch for: Pain at the back knee. Tip: Use blocks under your hands or drop the back knee to ease off.

Frog Stretch.cue: Knees wide, rock the hips back with a neutral spine.
Frog Stretch.howTo: Setup: On hands and knees, widen your knees and keep your feet in line. Move: Rock your hips back toward your heels. Watch for: Discomfort in the knees. Tip: Pad your knees. Gentle inner-thigh stretch.

Quadruped Rock-Back.cue: Keep the spine neutral and rock the hips toward the heels.
Quadruped Rock-Back.howTo: Setup: On hands and knees. Move: Sit your hips back toward your heels, keeping your spine neutral, then return. Watch for: Rounding your back. Tip: Gentle hip and ankle mobility.

Cobra Stretch.cue: Hips on the floor, press up gently through the chest.
Cobra Stretch.howTo: Setup: Lie face down with your hands beside your chest. Move: Press up gently, lifting your chest while keeping your hips down. Watch for: Pinching in the low back. Tip: Go only as high as comfortable.

Lat Stretch.cue: Reach long, ribs down, sit the hips back.
Lat Stretch.howTo: Setup: Hold a post, rack, or door frame at hip height, arms straight. Move: Sit your hips back and drop your chest until you feel the stretch along your side and back. Hold 30 seconds. Watch for: Arching. Tip: Breathe into your armpit.

Calf Stretch.cue: Heel down with a straight knee, then bend the knee for the soleus.
Calf Stretch.howTo: Setup: Face a wall with one foot back, hands on the wall. Move: Keep the back heel down and the back knee straight, lean forward until you feel the stretch in the upper calf. Bend that knee slightly to reach the lower calf. Hold 30 seconds. Watch for: The back heel lifting. Tip: Breathe slowly; do not bounce.

Figure-Four Stretch.cue: Ankle across the knee and pull the thigh toward the chest.
Figure-Four Stretch.howTo: Setup: Lie on your back, cross one ankle over the opposite knee. Move: Pull the lower thigh toward your chest until you feel a stretch in the outer hip. Hold 30 seconds. Watch for: Strain in the knee. Tip: Good alternative to pigeon.

Standing Quad Stretch.cue: Knees together, tuck the pelvis and pull the heel to the glute.
Standing Quad Stretch.howTo: Setup: Stand holding a wall for balance. Move: Grab your ankle and pull your heel toward your glute, knees together. Hold 30 seconds. Watch for: Arching. Tip: Squeeze the glute to deepen it.

Thoracic Extension on Foam Roller.cue: Roller across the mid-back, hands behind the head, extend gently.
Thoracic Extension on Foam Roller.howTo: Setup: Lie with a foam roller across your upper back, hands behind your head. Move: Gently extend back over the roller, then return. Move the roller up or down a few inches. Watch for: Low back arching. Tip: Support your head. No roller? Use a rolled towel.

Jefferson Curl.cue: Light load, curl the spine down one segment at a time.
Jefferson Curl.howTo: Setup: Stand on a low box or floor with no weight. Move: Slowly roll down through the spine one segment at a time, then roll back up. Watch for: Rushing or adding load. Tip: Advanced; go bodyweight only.

Spiderman Stretch.cue: Step into a deep lunge, hand inside, rotate and reach up.
Spiderman Stretch.howTo: Setup: Start in a plank position. Move: Step one foot beside your hand, sink your hips, and return. Watch for: Rushing. Tip: Hold briefly in the bottom.

Terminal Knee Extension.cue: Soft knee, straighten fully against the resistance and squeeze the quad.
Terminal Knee Extension.howTo: Setup: Place a band behind your knee or use a cable at knee height, standing with a soft knee. Move: Straighten your knee fully against the resistance and squeeze the quad, then ease back. Watch for: Locking out forcefully. Tip: Light resistance. This is a knee-friendly way to wake up the quads.

Clamshell.cue: Hips stacked, feet together, lift the top knee without rolling back.
Clamshell.howTo: Setup: Lie on your side with knees bent and feet together, a band around the thighs if you like. Move: Lift your top knee while keeping your feet touching, without rolling your hips back, then lower slowly. Watch for: Rolling the pelvis backward. Tip: You should feel it in the side of your hip.

Curl-Up.cue: Lift only the head and shoulders, hold briefly, and keep the low back still.
Curl-Up.howTo: Setup: Lie on your back with one knee bent and hands under your low back. Move: Lift your head and shoulders slightly and hold, then lower. Watch for: Pulling on your neck. Tip: A spine-friendly alternative to the sit-up.

Fist Push-Up.cue: Keep the wrists straight and lower the chest between the hands.
Fist Push-Up.howTo: Setup: Make fists and place your knuckles on the floor under your shoulders, wrists straight. Move: Lower your chest between your fists with your elbows at about 45 degrees, then press up. Watch for: Letting your wrists bend. Tip: A friendly option if flat-hand push-ups bother your wrists. Put a folded towel under your knuckles if the floor is hard.

Elliptical Trainer.cue: Stand tall and keep smooth, even strides.
Elliptical Trainer.howTo: Setup: Stand upright with feet flat on the pedals. Move: Stride smoothly, pushing and pulling the handles. Watch for: Leaning on the handles. Tip: Low impact and easy on the joints.
